hooks.text: In March 1888, mild spring weather instantly became a blinding whiteout.
Up to fifty foot snowdrifts paralyzed New York City in 1888.
Why did a spring morning suddenly freeze New York City in 1888?

title: How Did an 1888 Spring Morning Freeze New York? ❄️
description: Commuters stepped into unseasonably mild spring weather just hours before a sudden whiteout blizzard froze New York City in its tracks in March 1888.

beats.text: In March 1888, mild spring weather instantly became a blinding whiteout.

beats.text: Heavy rains rapidly turned to snow as temperatures plunged after midnight.

beats.text: Winds whipped snowdrifts up to fifty feet high across New York City.

beats.text: Thousands of commuters were trapped on frozen elevated train lines.

beats.text: Over two hundred people froze to death after stepping into the storm.

beats.text: The disaster forced city leaders to build transit lines permanently underground.
